terms.gloss: write something, drop me a line
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.38.2: sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis
Traupman 102: scrībe aliquid litterārum quandō vacās
terms.comment: Cicero to Atticus: the future scrībēs works as a friendly imperative.

phrases.latin: tū, quoniam necesse nihil est, sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis
phrases.english: since there’s no need, just drop me a line if you have time
Drop me a line when you have time.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 102.
Cic. Att. 12.38.2 from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the edition named there.
